items.title: Blackstone's Gray Says AI Infrastructure Is 'Right Place to Be'
items.summary: Blackstone President Jonathan Gray says he is positive about the outlook for the artificial intelligence buildout even as the cost of capital rises. "When I look back at this versus other periods of access, like the telecom boom where people built supply ahead of demand, where there was a ton of leverage, this looks and feels very different," Gray tells Yvonne Man on the sidelines of the Bloomberg New Economy Forum in New Delhi. (Source: Bloomberg)

items.title: Barclays: “Generational Shift” in Aerospace & Defense
items.summary: Anthony Valentini of Barclays says aerospace and defense is at an inflection point: newer, high-growth companies using commercial business models should be evaluated differently from traditional contractors and could achieve higher margins at scale. He describes the shift toward lower-cost autonomous systems as a generational change, with new entrants positioned to gain market share over the next decade. He speaks with Scarlet Fu & Hema Parmar on "The Close." (Source: Bloomberg)

items.title: Neocloud Prime Intellect Acquires Startup To Speed Up Inference
items.summary: Neoclouds and so-called inference providers that help app developers run open source models are trying to differentiate themselves in a very crowded market. For instance, one such neocloud, Prime Intellect , which was valued at $1 billion in an equity financing in July, is buying a startup to help it make open models run faster and more cheaply on its Nvidia servers, compared to its rivals. Prime Intellect, based in San Francisco, is acquiring Moondream , a young developer of open-source models that has fewer than 10 employees, according to Prime Intellect co-founder and CEO Vincent Weisser . (Weisser wouldn’t share the terms of the deal, but Moondream has raised $4.5 million in funding.) San Francisco- and Seattle-based Moondream is best known for an open-source vision-language model for analyzing and understanding images, like identifying boxes in an image of a warehouse or ads in a livestream. But Prime Intellect is largely acquiring the startup for its employees’ skills in writing software to make models run more efficiently, Weisser said.

This time, it was Meta Platforms’ turn, unveiling Muse Wonder, which it claims can “deliver state-of-the-art performance” on certain tasks. It was a triumphant moment for the company, whose AI efforts previously went through a slump that prompted a massive hiring binge over the past 14 months or so. It now claims it is “pushing the frontier” of AI. That would be notable if only everyone wasn’t claiming to be doing the same thing. Two weeks ago, Google unveiled its latest model, Gemini 4 Argon, which it says “delivers frontier performance in complex workflows” across various subjects (you wouldn’t want it to deliver frontier performance in simple workflows, would you?). In early September, OpenAI announced GPT-6 Astra , which it said was “state of the art on computer use, browsing, software engineering, cybersecurity, science and professional work.” Also in September, Anthropic introduced Claude Fable 5.1 and Mythos 5.1 , which it claimed to be “the world’s most advanced models for coding and knowledge work.”
